label: Form, equality, exaltation and attribution in Philippians 2
term: form, equality, exaltation and attribution in Philippians 2
resolution: The new propositions encode the letter’s third-person assertions, not Jesus’s actual self-claims, historical events or the case signature’s actual divine identity. Form is lexical and is not identified with Aristotelian form or the Creed’s consubstantiality; equality is not an identity equation. Harpagmos alternatives and preexistent-divine versus commissioned-agent accounts remain distinct in docs/philippians-christology.md. God’s exaltation of Christ and homage to the Father’s glory retain the textual distinction without deciding its ontology. Neither theological truth nor a report-to-history bridge follows from the attribution.
